messages:

Subject: VPC pricing question: amortizing platform fee for a 12‑month pilot

Hi Markus —

Thanks again for the demo last week. Medilabs is excited to move forward with a VPC/private deployment for our inference workloads. Before we get legal/procurement involved I wanted to clarify a couple of commercial points so we can scope the PO:

- We expect an initial pilot (12 months) starting with 4 dedicated nodes (NVIDIA A10x or equivalent), ramping to 8 nodes after month 3.
- Our procurement team is keen to amortize the platform fee across the first 12 months (rather than one‑time), and they'd like to understand Redwood's flexibility on that for an initial contract.
- Support tier: we need 24x7 critical incident support for production go‑live, but during pilot we can accept business hours for noncritical issues. Is a tiered support band possible (pilot vs. post‑go‑live) without re‑signing a new SOW?

Attached is our standard procurement form to speed things along. Can you share a modeled example of amortizing the platform fee + any starter credits you might extend for first 12 months?

Thanks — happy to hop on a quick call this week if that helps.

Best,
Sarah Cho
Head of AI Ops, Medilabs
attachments: Medilabs_Procurement_Form.docx
From: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>

Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 05 Jan 2026 13:30:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: VPC pricing question: amortizing platform fee for a 12‑month pilot

Hi Sarah —

Great to hear Medilabs is ready to pilot. Short answers up front, then options:

1) Platform fee amortization: yes, we can spread the platform fee across the initial contract term as an invoiced monthly line item. Two common approaches:
   - Amortize the full platform fee over the 12 months (monthly platform fee line).
   - Apply a starter credit that reduces the first 3–6 months’ platform fee, then revert to list monthly platform fee.

2) Support tiers: we can offer a pilot support band (business hours, priority queue) that converts to 24x7 critical coverage upon go‑live. That conversion can be handled by the SOW (no new signature required if the SOW includes a conversion clause).

3) Tradeoffs: amortization increases monthly cashflow flexibility for you but means Redwood carries the up‑front deferral; starter credits are easier for us to control but are time‑bound.

I attached a draft term sheet with two amortization schedules and a sample starter credit (one‑time credit equal to 20% of the first 3 months’ platform fee). Please note the numbers are illustrative — if you confirm expected steady‑state token volumes and SLA needs I can run a more exact model.

Proposed next step: I’ll get Rishi to run a quick cost model and propose a recommendation (amortize vs credit) and a suggested discounted band for a 12‑month pilot + conversion to enterprise.

— Markus
VP, Sales — Redwood Inference

Thanks Markus — that helps. A few clarifications from procurement/finance:

- Expected steady‑state (after month 3): ~4M tokens/day across the cluster (inference only).
- We can commit to an 80% utilization baseline for the first 12 months.
- Budget prefers platform fee amortization, but any starter credit combination is acceptable if the total TCO is similar (we prefer predictability).
- Can you confirm whether the starter credit affects the SLA (i.e., reduced credit means different SLO)?

We reviewed the term sheet — two asks:
1) Can you show a monthly amortization schedule with the platform fee spread and the per‑node onprem SKU line?
2) If Redwood offers a 15% discount on the platform fee for a 12‑month pilot (in exchange for a 12‑month minimum commitment and a PO signed within 10 business days), will Medilabs get conversion pricing guarantees upon renewal?

If we can get those answers this week, procurement can prepare the PO.

— Sarah

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>

Date: Thu, 08 Jan 2026 10:15:00 -08:00
Subject: Fwd: Medilabs amortization request — cost model attached

Markus / Lauren —

Forwarding my quick cost model + recommendation. Key points:

- Baseline platform fee (list): $120k/year.
- Amortize over 12 months -> $10k/month. With expected utilization and node counts the net per‑token unit cost moves in your favor compared to hosted.
- Starter credit option: one‑time $24k credit applied against first 3 months (effectively 20% of first‑year platform fee).
- Discounting: for a firm 12‑month PO signed within 10 business days, we can offer an additional 10% off platform fee (stackable with amortization) OR a 15% off if Medilabs allows a 6‑week onboarding window where we co‑deliver runbook work (operational uplift).

Recommendation: Offer amortization + 10% early‑sign discount + 3‑month starter credit. This keeps cashflow neutral for Medilabs while limiting Redwood exposure.

Attached: Cost_Model_V1.xlsx (monthly amortization table + per‑node SKU breakout). I flagged line items that require legal approval (non‑standard conversion clause).

— Rishi
Sr. Director, Commercial

Thanks — that model is helpful. Short confirmation on mechanics we can commit to today pending legal/SOW: 

- Amortization: Redwood will invoice platform fee monthly across the 12‑month pilot term (we will reflect this as a monthly line on the invoice).
- Early sign discount: 10% platform fee discount if PO signed within 10 business days from the date of this email.
- Starter credit: $24k one‑time credit applied in month 1–3 as agreed.
- Support: Pilot support = business hours priority; conversion to 24x7 critical incident support upon declared production go‑live (conversion per SOW clause, no new signature required).

I'll ask legal to prepare an SOW with the conversion clause and the amortization wording. Once that's attached to the PO we should be able to proceed. I'll generate a DocuSign term‑sheet link and include the cost model and redlines for your procurement team.
